questions.title: Two Sum — the right lookup
questions.question: You must find two numbers that add up to a target. Which approach turns the naive O(n²) scan into a single pass?
options: Sort the array first, then binary search
Store seen values in a hash map and look up target − current
Compare every pair with nested loops
Use a stack of all elements
questions.explanation: A hash map gives O(1) average lookups, so for each element you can instantly check whether its complement (target − current) was already seen — one pass, O(n) time.

questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeats
questions.question: To find the longest substring with all-unique characters, which technique avoids re-checking characters?
options: Generate every substring and test each
A sliding window with a set, shrinking from the left on a duplicate
questions.explanation: A sliding window keeps a set of the current window's characters; on a duplicate you advance the left edge until it's unique again. Each character enters and leaves the window once → O(n).

questions.title: Valid Parentheses
questions.question: Which data structure naturally validates correctly-nested brackets like '([{}])'?
questions.explanation: A stack matches the last-opened / first-closed (LIFO) nature of nesting: push openers, and on each closer pop and check it matches. Empty stack at the end means balanced.

questions.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
questions.question: Merging two sorted linked lists into one sorted list is most cleanly done by…
options: Copying both into an array and sorting
Walking both with two pointers, always attaching the smaller head
A hash map of node values
questions.explanation: Both inputs are already sorted, so a two-pointer merge attaches the smaller current node each step — O(n+m) time and O(1) extra space, no re-sorting needed.

questions.title: Max Depth of a Binary Tree
questions.question: What is the cleanest way to compute the maximum depth of a binary tree?
questions.explanation: Depth is defined recursively: an empty tree is 0, otherwise it's 1 plus the deeper of the two subtrees. This visits each node once → O(n).

questions.title: Best Time to Buy & Sell Stock
questions.question: For one buy and one later sell maximizing profit, what do you track in a single pass?
options: The minimum price so far and the best profit so far
The maximum price so far only
A sorted copy of the prices
questions.explanation: Keep the lowest price seen so far; at each day the best sale is price − minSoFar. Track the max of those. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.

questions.title: Contains Duplicate
questions.question: What's the most efficient way to detect if any value repeats in an array?
options: Insert into a hash set and stop if a value already exists
Sort then compare neighbors, always the best choice
questions.explanation: A hash set gives O(1) average membership checks: stream the values in and return true the moment one is already present — O(n) time. (Sorting works too but is O(n log n).)

questions.title: Climbing Stairs
questions.question: Ways to climb n stairs taking 1 or 2 steps at a time follow which pattern?
options: The Fibonacci recurrence: ways(n) = ways(n−1) + ways(n−2)
questions.explanation: The last move is either a single or double step, so ways(n) = ways(n−1) + ways(n−2) — Fibonacci. Compute bottom-up with two rolling variables in O(n).

questions.title: Invert a Binary Tree
questions.question: Inverting (mirroring) a binary tree is done by…
options: Swapping left and right children at every node
questions.explanation: Mirroring means every node's left and right subtrees swap. Recurse, swapping children at each node — O(n), visiting each node once.

questions.title: Maximum Subarray
questions.question: Kadane's algorithm finds the maximum-sum contiguous subarray by…
options: At each index, keeping the better of (extend previous sum) vs (start fresh)
Using a hash map of prefix sums only
questions.explanation: Kadane tracks a running best-ending-here: current = max(num, current + num), and the answer is the max of those. Extending vs restarting is the key decision → O(n).

questions.title: Valid Anagram
questions.question: The fastest general check that two strings are anagrams uses…
options: Checking the first and last characters
questions.explanation: Anagrams have identical character counts. Tally each string's frequencies (a hash map or 26-size array) and compare — O(n). Sorting also works but is O(n log n).

questions.title: Clone Graph
questions.question: When deep-copying a graph with cycles, what prevents infinite loops?
options: A visited map from original node → its clone
questions.explanation: A map from each original node to its clone lets you reuse already-created copies instead of re-cloning, which both handles cycles and wires up shared neighbors correctly.
